summary.short: Sets duties of care for providers of UK-linked user-to-user and search services to assess and mitigate risks of illegal content and content harmful to children, and gives OFCOM regulatory functions, codes of practice and enforcement powers.
summary.long: The Act imposes duties of care on providers of UK-linked user-to-user and search services to assess and mitigate risks of illegal content and content harmful to children (ss. 9-12, 26-29). Category 1 services face further duties on user empowerment, democratic and journalistic content and impact assessments (ss. 14-19, 22). Services must run complaints procedures, keep records and publish terms of service and transparency reports (ss. 20-23, 71-72, 77). Services likely to be accessed by children must carry out access assessments (ss. 35-37); pornographic internet services must ensure children are not normally able to encounter such content (s. 81). Fraudulent advertising duties apply to Category 1 and 2A services (ss. 38-40). CSEA content must be reported to the NCA; knowingly false reports are an offence punishable by up to 2 years' imprisonment on indictment or a fine (ss. 66, 69). OFCOM issues codes of practice recommending compliance measures (ss. 41-50), and regulated services must notify OFCOM for fee-paying years (s. 83). The fetched text covers Parts 1-6 to s. 83(4); Parts 7-12 are not included.
